elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates..." — express defence duty running to Company and affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)..."

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Site or any services or deliverables provided by HDI infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — tracks the Site/services/deliverables scope of this development-and-hosting agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of the Company's data or Confidential Information caused by HDI".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "The Company shall defend and indemnify HDI against third-party claims to the extent arising out of the Content provided by the Company or the Company's breach of applicable law" — two narrow triggers only, no broader Customer indemnity for HDI's services.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-party claims.
elements.evidence: Element text as supplied reads 'Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims'; limb (a) of the inserted paragraph covers third-party IP infringement/misappropriation allegations regarding the Site and HDI's services and deliverables.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; the inserted indemnity contains no modification carve-out, which is more protective of Customer, so the permitted exclusion condition simply does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination carve-out is included, leaving broader Customer protection, so nothing to satisfy.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-specification carve-out was inserted, which is Customer-favourable.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no procure/modify/replace remedy ladder for infringing Site or services.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop appears in the inserted language or elsewhere in Section 9.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap is stated; the drafter deliberately omitted it (rationale acknowledges this).

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements appear in operative inserted text (defence + indemnity for Company and affiliates; IP, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs; notice, control and cooperation mechanics; and a Customer indemnity narrowed to Company-provided Content and Company's breach of law).

Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met; omitting the super-cap is also correct here since the Agreement has no general liability cap and adding one would gratuitously limit HDI's exposure.

Minimality holds: the change is a single concise insertion of an absent clause placed after the warranty section; no existing language (including the Customer-favourable Globix carve-out in 9(b)) is deleted or paraphrased, and no extras beyond the checklist (no survival tail, no at-own-expense wording, no added damages categories, no settlement-consent or expense procedures) were added. The 'hold harmless' and 'damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)' wording is ordinary indemnity formulation required to make the indemnity operative.
Intent preserved: unrelated allocation, timing and commercial mechanics are untouched, no cross-reference is broken, and the reciprocal Customer indemnity does not contradict any retained sentence.

Two cosmetic points to tidy on the next pass, neither a defect in substance: (i) the inserted paragraph carries no section number and sits between 9(b) and Section 10 — number it 9(c) or as a new Section 10 with renumbering to avoid a citation gap; and (ii) confirm that "Content" is a capitalised defined term elsewhere in the Agreement, and if it is not, change it to "content provided by the Company" so the Customer-side indemnity does not turn on an undefined term.
